title: Spiking the mind: Rethinking the role of cortical feedback in visual mental imagery.
title_zh: 尖峰成像：重新思考皮层反馈在视觉意象中的作用
abstract: Recent research has revealed similarities between visual mental imagery and visual perception. Visual imagery is supported by cortical feedback involving multiple visual areas, including the primary visual cortex, and functionally interacts with perception. This has led to the assumption that imagery is "perception in reverse," with feedback connections driving action potentials in early visual areas. However, evidence on feedback mechanisms is mixed, often exerting modulation (often as negative gain control) in sensory areas. Here, we examine and interpret the current understanding of feedback mechanisms related to visual imagery, integrating this with its functional effects and neural correlates. Finally, we put forward a new hypothesis, along with testable predictions, proposing that imagery reshapes spontaneous neural activity rather than producing spiking in early visual areas. This new framework explains many of the properties of visual imagery while providing a better general understanding of feedback and brain function. abstract_zh: 近期研究揭示了视觉意象与视觉感知之间的相似性。视觉意象受到涉及多个视觉区域（包括初级视觉皮层）的皮层反馈支持，并与感知产生功能性相互作用。这导致人们假设意象是“反向感知”，即反馈连接驱动早期视觉区域产生动作电位。然而，关于反馈机制的证据尚无定论，反馈常常对感觉区域产生调制作用（通常表现为负增益控制）。在此，我们考察并诠释了与视觉意象相关的反馈机制的现有认知，并将其与功能效应和神经相关性相结合。最后，我们提出了一项新假设及可检验的预测，认为意象重塑自发神经活动，而非在早期视觉区域产生尖峰。这一新框架解释了视觉意象的许多特性，并对反馈和脑功能提供了更佳的普遍理解。（PsycInfo 数据库记录（c）2026 APA，版权所有。）
